references.text: The prophet Isaiah urges Israel to shine with God's glory, illuminating the darkness around the nations, parallel to how Jesus describes his followers as the light of the world.
The psalm describes God's word as a lamp for the feet and a light on the path, resembling the image of Jesus' followers as the light in the world.
Jesus calls himself the light of the world, which underscores his disciples' role as bearers of light in the world.
Jesus again affirms that he is the light of the world, providing context for his statement in Matthew that his followers are also the light of the world.
Paul urges the Ephesians to live as lights in the Lord, reflecting Jesus' instructions in Matthew.
Peter's letter describes believers as a chosen people, called out of darkness into his wonderful light, parallel to the image of light in Matthew.
